summary.title: Securing Jenkins
summary.one_liner: Learn which Jenkins security options exist (controller isolation, access control, CSRF, CSP, markup formatters, user content rendering) and which must be configured for your environment.
takeaways: Builds should not run on the built-in node, and the controller should be isolated from build workloads.
Jenkins denies anonymous access by default and has a single admin user; the setup wizard configures access control securely.
CSRF protection and the default markup formatter are secure by default, while CSP and access control for builds depend on environment needs.
Content served from workspaces and artifacts is strictly limited by default; HTML reports can be enabled carefully.
Some features (CSP, build access control, environment variable handling) need deliberate configuration and carry trade-offs.
summary.summary: This official Jenkins documentation chapter is an overview of the security options available to Jenkins administrators and users. It lists sub-sections covering controller isolation, access control, builds, environment variables, organization folder and multibranch pipeline credentials, CSRF protection, Content Security Policy, markup formatters, and rendering user content. For each, it notes whether the default is secure, or whether the setting must be tuned to the environment. It is a conceptual guide and does not give step-by-step configuration commands in the text provided.
